lines.trans: Our studio just put out several new releases again.
Are these actually any good? Look, even you don't sound confident.
Making tons of tapes is fine, yet I want to see one powerhouse hit.
Honestly, unless you release a new Kuroki film or find her equal, things will get tough.
This right here is a communications satellite floating in outer space.
Mr. Kawada, do you think the day will come when adult videos air on Japanese television?
Well, with regulations and everything, I think that would be difficult.
Every human goes through painful times—what is wrong with bringing people joy!
Still, satellites cost enormous money, which is why we must raise funds.
Volume is fine, yet we also need to make a true flagship film.
Increase our production budgets fivefold, please.
If regulations stand in our way, let's go somewhere with no regulations!

meanings.note: Checks agreement ('isn't it?') or softens a request or farewell.
Used in everyday farewells like またね, また明日, and また会いましょう.

examples.text: また明日会いましょう。

meanings.note: Marks the subject of existence, emergence, or questions (どれが), and at the end of a polite clause softens a request (のですが).

examples.text: お願いがあるのですが。
examples.trans: I have a favor to ask.

meanings.note: All-purpose action verb; turns Sino-Japanese nouns into verbs (融通する, 出店する) and with に means 'decide on' or 'make into'.
Tells the listener something new or adds warm reassurance at the end of a sentence.
Standalone pronoun ('this'), unlike この which requires a noun.
Plain い-adjective.

examples.text: この映画はとても面白いです。
何か面白い話はありませんか。
examples.trans: Do you have any interesting stories?

meanings.note: Links a modifying noun to a following noun, or turns a clause into an explanatory statement (often contracted to ん in speech).

examples.text: これって面白いの？ほら、自信なさげ。
examples.trans: Are these actually any good? Look, even you don't sound confident.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.en: casual reflection or firm reminder particle
meanings.note: Used aloud to oneself ('man, I'm hungry') or at the end of a warning ('remember that, okay?').

meanings.en: go forward; work out well (いけます = 'it will work!')
meanings.note: Written in kana for figurative headway: いけます! ('this can go / this will work!'), 思いどおりにいかない ('does not go as hoped').

examples.text: この企画ならいけます！
examples.trans: With this plan, it will work!

examples.text: 仕事がうまくいっています。

examples.trans: All of our satellite lines are already full.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Marks the presence of a person (責任者はいるか) or follows て-form (often contracted to てる/てます in speech).
Used both to answer yes politely and when handing an item to someone.
Limits the preceding noun or phrase to that item alone.

examples.text: これだけお願いします。
いっぱい作るのはいいんだけど、強い一発を見てえんだよ。
examples.trans: Making tons of tapes is fine, yet I want to see one powerhouse hit.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Written を and pronounced o; marks what an action directly acts upon.
Ichidan verb: blunt imperative 見ろ ('look!') is rough command speech.

examples.text: お前ら、観光じゃないんだからしっかりしろよ。
examples.trans: Hey, this isn't sightseeing, so pull yourselves together.

examples.text: 彼女は来るんだろうな？
ちゃんとキャストはそろってるんだろうな？
examples.trans: You've got the whole cast properly lined up, right?

meanings.en: open a store; bring out; hand in
meanings.note: 店を出す means opening a branch; 出しやがって attaches tough-guy disdainful やがる.

examples.text: 駅前に新しい店を出します。
examples.trans: We open a new branch in front of the station.

examples.text: 書類を出してください。

meanings.note: Turns a statement into a question, or softens a volitional/negative guess.

examples.text: 正直、黒木香の新作を出すか替わる誰かを見つけないと厳しいよ。
examples.trans: Honestly, unless you release a new Kuroki film or find her equal, things will get tough.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Negates verbs or forms じゃない ('is not') in questions like いいんじゃないか.

meanings.en: as for; topic or contrast marker
meanings.note: Written は but pronounced wa when marking the topic or contrasting one item with another.

examples.text: これは宇宙空間にある通信衛星だ。
examples.trans: This right here is a communications satellite floating in outer space.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.en: target, location of existence, or result marker
meanings.note: Marks destination, location where something exists or sits, or the chosen result before する and なる.

meanings.en: exist; be available; remain in place
meanings.note: Used for inanimate things and abstract concepts; after て-form (書いてある, 置いてある) describes a resulting state left in place.

examples.text: 名前が書いてあります。
これは宇宙空間にある通信衛星だ。
examples.trans: This right here is a communications satellite floating in outer space.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Plain sentence-ending copula; contracts or shifts to だった in past, だろう/だろ for supposition, and で/じゃ in combinations.
Attached to surnames, given names, or company names to show everyday respect; never used for oneself.
Read にほん (Nihon) or にっぽん (Nippon).

examples.text: 日本の文化が好きです。
村西監督、テレビ出演おめでとう！
examples.trans: Director Muranishi, congratulations on your television appearance!

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

examples.text: その日が来たら一週間はバラエティ番組の放送を見送らせる。
examples.trans: When that day arrives, networks will suspend variety broadcasts for one week.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.en: location of action; means; scope total
meanings.note: Marks where an action happens, the unit/scope of a rate or total (十日で, 全部で), or the cause/occasion.

examples.trans: It is one thousand yen in total.

examples.text: その日が来たら一週間はバラエティ番組の放送を見送らせる。
examples.trans: When that day arrives, networks will suspend variety broadcasts for one week.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

できる.gloss: be built; open; be able to

meanings.en: come into existence; be completed; can do
meanings.note: With buildings or stores (店ができる), means a new shop has been built or opened.

examples.text: 駅前に新しいカフェができました。
examples.trans: A new café opened in front of the station.

examples.text: 日本語が少しできます。
examples.trans: I can speak a little Japanese.

meanings.note: Irregular verb: くる -> きます -> きました.

meanings.en: to think; to feel; to believe
meanings.note: Often follows quotative と to express an opinion or belief.

examples.text: それはいいと思います。

meanings.note: Softens a refusal or correction at the start of a reply.
Plain い-adjective.

examples.text: この問題は少し難しいです。
examples.trans: This problem is a little difficult.

examples.text: あまり難しく考えないでください。

meanings.note: Refers to humans in general or human nature.

examples.text: 人間には表と裏がある。
examples.trans: Human beings have a public face and a hidden side.

meanings.note: Colloquial particle adding emphasis, similar to でも or も.

examples.text: 俺だって言いたいことがある。
examples.trans: I have something I want to say too.

examples.text: 誰だって間違いはある。

meanings.note: Attaches to pronouns or people nouns (僕ら, 彼ら).
Read なん before だ/です/の, and なに before が/を or alone.

examples.text: 何を買いにきましたか。
examples.trans: What did you come to buy?

meanings.en: bad; sorry (in past 悪かった)
meanings.note: Casual past 悪かったな admits fault ('that was bad of me / my bad').

examples.text: 今日は天気が悪いです。
しかしこれには莫大な金がかかる。だから資金調達が必要なんです。
examples.trans: Still, satellites cost enormous money, which is why we must raise funds.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

examples.text: 俺も金なんとか集めるからよ。もうちょっと明るくやろうや。
examples.trans: I'll scrape together some money too, so let's keep our spirits up.

examples.text: ああ。リスクもあるが、懸けてみるか、トシ。
examples.trans: Yeah. There's risk involved too, though—ready to take the gamble, Toshi?

examples.text: 強制送還の金がかかるだけで、何の見せしめにもならないだろ？
examples.trans: Deporting them just costs money and doesn't serve as an example to anyone, right?

examples.text: しかしこれには莫大な金がかかる。だから資金調達が必要なんです。
examples.trans: Still, satellites cost enormous money, which is why we must raise funds.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Used with が before it (ストーリーが必要だ 'a story is needed') or な before a noun.
Everyday spoken counterpart of なぜ or どうして.

examples.text: なんで知っているんですか。
数もいいんですけど、もっと看板になるような作品も作らないと。
examples.trans: Volume is fine, yet we also need to make a true flagship film.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Replaces は, が, or を to add 'also' or 'too'.

examples.trans: Please give me this one too.

examples.text: あそこも新しい店です。
examples.trans: Over there is a new shop too.

meanings.note: Irregular i-adjective whose past/conditional stems use よ- (よかったら).

examples.text: よかったら来てください。

meanings.note: Intensifies the following adverb or verb, as in もっとちゃんと見て.

examples.text: もっと近くで見てください。
もっとゆっくり話してください。

meanings.note: Expresses change of state, or in polite customer service (になります) states an arrangement or price total.

examples.trans: That comes to one thousand yen.

meanings.note: Between の and な (あなたのような人), describes someone or something 'like ...'.

examples.text: 春のような暖かい日です。
examples.trans: It is a warm day like spring.

examples.text: あなたのような人を探していました。
examples.trans: I was looking for someone like you.

examples.text: 制作費はこれまでの五倍かけて量産していくぞ！
examples.trans: We will spend five times our previous budget and mass-produce!

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

examples.text: 制作費はこれまでの五倍かけて量産していくぞ！
examples.trans: We will spend five times our previous budget and mass-produce!

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

examples.text: 今店舗を増やして急成長してる店に掛け合ってみるんだ。
examples.trans: I will negotiate with a chain that is adding stores and growing fast right now.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Follows a verb's て-form or polite お + stem (お待ちください, お持ち帰りください) to make a polite request.

examples.text: ここに書いてください。

なら.gloss: if it is; in the case of

meanings.note: Conditional topic marker placed right after a noun or pronoun (あなたなら 'if it were you').

examples.text: あなたならどうしますか？
examples.trans: If it were you, what would you do?

examples.text: 明日なら時間があります。
examples.trans: If it is tomorrow, I have time.
